theorems.label: agent-proof
theorems.name: Pure-power theorem (the dominant balance at a pole is w^(K) = lambda*w^n and nothing else)

hypotheses.text: the equation is solved for the highest derivative: E = c*wK - Phi(w0, ..., w_{K-1}), c != 0 constant
hypotheses.how: c = L**2; for generic parameter values

hypotheses.text: Phi = lambda*w0**n + Psi with n >= 2 and lambda != 0
hypotheses.how: n = 3, lambda = -2*Q**2; for generic parameter values

hypotheses.text: (H): every monomial of Psi has weight sum e_j*(p + j) < n*p, where p = K/(n - 1)
hypotheses.how: p = 1, n*p = 3; largest weight of a monomial of Psi: 2

theorems.conclusion: every meromorphic solution is rational, simply periodic (a rational function of one exponential exp(a*z), a != 0) or elliptic
theorems.source: project note (not yet public): 'Meromorphic solutions of equations whose dominant balance at a pole is a pure power', Theorem 1; for the bound on the number of Laurent series a second project note (not yet public), Theorem 4.6 — first note: Theorem 1, hypothesis (H), paragraph 'Consequence for the classification of solutions', Lemmas 2, 4, 6, Remark 2; second note: Theorem 4.6 (bound), Theorem 5.1

theorems.name: Eremenko's theorem (finiteness property and one monomial of top degree)

hypotheses.text: E is a polynomial in w and its derivatives with constant coefficients
hypotheses.how: by construction of the Equation object

hypotheses.text: E has exactly one monomial of the largest total degree
hypotheses.how: total degree 3; the only monomial of this degree is w0**3 (coefficient 2*L**2*Q**2); for generic parameter values

hypotheses.text: finiteness property: only finitely many formal Laurent series with a pole satisfy the equation
hypotheses.how: the Laurent series at p = 1 contain arbitrary coefficients (positive integer Fuchs indices with satisfied compatibility conditions)

theorems.conclusion: every meromorphic solution is rational, simply periodic (a rational function of one exponential exp(a*z), a != 0) or elliptic, with at most N poles in a period
theorems.source: A. Eremenko, Meromorphic traveling wave solutions of the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, J. Math. Phys. Anal. Geom. 2 (2006) 278-286; arXiv:nlin/0504053 — Theorem 2, p. 282 (general statement); Theorem 1, p. 279 (the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky reduction, with proof)

basis.label: agent-proof
basis.text: Theorem P: Lemmas 5.1-5.5 of project note; eliminations for the two- and three-pole functions with symbolic theta (Singular, char 0). The cases r_i = 0 are Ng-Wu 2019 (Theorem 1.5, read by ORD2 in the local arXiv text) + demina_question Theorem 4.1 (re-proved); GENERAL section 4 proved that all solutions are group-type or twisted elliptic. The proof uses standard Nevanlinna tools (lemma on the logarithmic derivative, first main theorem), quoted and not read in this run. [LITCHECK: read: Ng-Wu 2019, Theorems 1.4-1.5 (pp. 5-6); Conte-Ng-Wu, Theorem 1 (p. 6)]

ruled_out.statement: Theorem P of project note: the nonconstant meromorphic solutions are exactly (1) fronts v' = A_i v^2 + B_i v + C_i when r_i = 0 (ORD2-P231-FRONT); (2) for A_i = 2 A_j, c + d A_i = 0: all solutions, v = -y'/(A_i y), y''' linear (ORD2-P231-COLEHOPF); (3) for A_j = -A_i/2, r_i = 0: logarithmic derivatives of the solutions of a type-(2,2,2) equation (ORD2-P231-FISHER-ELL, -TWIST0, -TWIST1); (4) for b = 0: all solutions if d = 0 (ORD2-P231-DUFFING-ELL) or if r_1 = r_2 = 0 (ORD2-P231-DUFFING-TWIST); (5) the two-pole waves on the codimension-two locus T (ORD2-P231-TWOPOLE). Elsewhere only constants (ORD2-P231-NOWAVE).

steps: divide by the coefficient of w2
shift w -> w + (M/(2*Q**2)) removes the term in w0**2
scale so that the coefficient of w0**3 is -2 and that of w0 is 1
radicals of the parameters are written as new parameters: rho1 = sqrt(-1/Q**2), rho2 = sqrt(L**2*Q**2/(-3*L**2*M**2 + 2*L**2*Q**2 + 2*Q**4))
normal_form.convention: monic in wK; shift kills the coefficient of m*/w0; coefficient of m* = T (a0 = 1 in the two-term balance); coefficient of the next monomial m1 = 1; see mero.transform
